title: Samsung Reportedly Hikes Chip Prices Amid TSMC Capacity Crunch: Nvidia, Apple, Tesla Fuel Demand
key_facts: Reuters reports, citing sources, that Samsung is raising prices on new orders for some advanced contract chipmaking services by up to 15%, with Chinese customers facing some of the steepest rises.
Sources say Samsung cannot accept all orders because it must serve US customers and keep capacity for its own chips.
Driver: TSMC is fully booked; its 3nm capacity is reportedly taken through 2026-2027 and its 2026 2nm output is claimed by Apple, Nvidia and AMD.
Samsung is the only other foundry able to make 2nm chips, so chip designers treat it as the overflow option.
Samsung already raised SF4 (4nm) prices in July by 10-15% for China and US customers and 5-10% for Taiwan; SF5 up 10-15%, 8nm up nearly 10%.
TSMC held over 70% of foundry revenue in Q1 2026 versus about 7% for Samsung (Counterpoint); TSMC was separately reported to be weighing a price rise of up to 10% from January 2027.
Google is in talks with Samsung for SF4 production, per a Reuters source; Meta was separately reported to be negotiating a $6.5 billion-plus 2nm order.
quote_evidence: According to a Reuters report, Samsung is increasing prices on new orders for some advanced contract chipmaking services, with Chinese customers facing some of the steepest increases.

According to Reuters, major fabless chip designers are increasingly treating Samsung as their only viable overflow option at the leading edge, since Samsung remains the only other foundry currently capable of 2nm production.
why_it_matters_hint: Advanced chip manufacturing is so short that the second-ranked foundry can now charge more and turn orders away.
event_date: Not stated precisely; Reuters report around 2-3 Oct 2026, July price rises cited as background
notes: Stocktwits relays Reuters; Reuters is the source. The Reuters report date is not given in the copy; premarket share move suggests Friday 2 Oct. Original Reuters link not given; url is the Stocktwits page.
